comment: The public roadmap. `bun nv site --check roadmap` keeps it in step with the goal chain, and `bun nv site --roadmap` copies it into README.md. `internal` lists the goals that are not public work.

themes.title: Debug records that stay within their limits
themes.text: The settings `index_age` and `index_max` under `[debug]` also delete the records of a finished run, oldest first. The run's page in the debug viewer shows which of its records were deleted.

themes.title: One setting for the certificates your server trusts
themes.text: A `[tls.client]` block sets which certificate authorities every outgoing TLS connection trusts. If a server's certificate comes from an unknown authority, the error names the setting that fixes it.

themes.title: Mail that a web app needs
themes.text: `Core\Mail` sends attachments, images inside the HTML, styled HTML, sender names and replies in a thread, through every common mail server. A program can also read a mailbox over IMAP. It can tell whether a message is a bounce, an automatic reply or a reply to a mail it sent.

themes.title: One way to change your code safely
themes.text: Each refactoring, such as a rename or a file move, checks its change before it writes it. The same refactorings work from your editor and from the command line with `nvs code`.

themes.title: Completion that offers only what your program can load
themes.text: Your editor suggests only the classes and namespaces that the program of the open file can load, plus `Core`.

themes.title: Test code and types that say what they mean
themes.text: `#[TestOnly]` marks a class or a method as test code. `nvs run` and `nvs build` leave it out, and code outside the tests cannot use it. A value tested with `is static` can be returned where the method returns `static`.
